question: Which of these measures of money supply is referred to as the aggregate monetary resources?
solution:
The correct answer is __**M3.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M3** is the measure of money supply that includes all the components of **M2 (currency, demand deposits, and time deposits)** as well as large-time **deposits,** repurchase **agreements,** and institutional **money market funds.**
 
• **M3** is often referred to as the **aggregate monetary resource** because it represents the broadest measure of money supply.
 
• **M4** is another measure of money supply that includes all the components of M3 as well as holdings of **money market instruments,** such as commercial paper and treasury bills.
 
• **MI, or monetary base**, is the narrowest measure of money supply and includes only currency in circulation and reserves held by **banks **at the central bank.
 
• **M2** is a broader measure of money supply than** MI.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **M4** is **not** as commonly used as the other measures of money supply.
 
• **MI **is often used as a tool for **monetary policy,** as changes in the monetary base can affect the amount of lending and borrowing in the economy.
 
• **M2** is often used as an** indicator of economic activity**, as the level of deposits in the economy can indicate the level of consumer and business spending.
 
• **M3** is often used as an indicator of **inflationary pressures,** as an increase in the money supply can lead to an increase in prices.
